Solids only
All states of matter
Fluids (liquids and gases) only

questions.explanation: Convection only occurs in fluids (liquids and gases) because it requires the bulk movement of particles, which cannot happen in solids where particles are fixed in position.

questions.stem: In convection, warm fluid rises because:

options.text: Heat always rises
Hot particles are lighter
It is pushed up by the cold fluid
It expands and becomes less dense than the surrounding cooler fluid

questions.explanation: When fluid is heated, it expands and becomes less dense. The less dense warm fluid rises above the denser cooler fluid, creating a convection current.

options.text: An electric current caused by heat
Heat transfer through a solid
A continuous circulation of fluid caused by differences in density
Electromagnetic radiation from a hot surface

questions.explanation: A convection current is a continuous circulation pattern in a fluid, driven by heating causing density differences -- warm fluid rises, cool fluid sinks to replace it.

questions.stem: Why are household radiators placed near the floor rather than the ceiling?

options.text: Because they work by conduction only
Because hot air sinks
So that heated air rises and sets up a convection current that warms the whole room
Because they look better at floor level

questions.explanation: Radiators at floor level heat the air around them. The warm air rises, cooler air moves in to replace it, and a convection current circulates warm air throughout the room.

questions.stem: Why does convection NOT occur in solids?

options.text: Solids do not have particles
Solids are too dense
Particles in solids cannot move freely from place to place
Solids cannot absorb heat

questions.explanation: Convection requires the bulk movement of particles. In solids, particles are fixed in position and can only vibrate, so they cannot move through the material to create convection currents.

questions.stem: Sea breezes during the day blow from the sea toward the land because:

options.text: The sea is warmer than the land during the day
Land heats up faster, warm air over land rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in
Water pushes the air toward land
The sea is always windy

questions.explanation: Land has a lower specific heat capacity than water, so it heats up faster. Warm air over the land rises, and cooler air from above the sea flows in to replace it, creating a sea breeze.

questions.stem: In a domestic hot water system, the heating element is placed at the bottom of the tank because:

options.text: Water at the bottom is heated, rises, and sets up a convection current to heat all the water
It is easier to install there
Hot water sinks to the bottom
The tank is stronger at the bottom

questions.explanation: Placing the heater at the bottom means hot water rises and cooler water sinks to be heated, creating a convection current that heats the entire tank efficiently.
